At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|12=draft|12=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * 社殿（2015th year ） |名称 = 月讀宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]中村町742-1[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area09.php 『式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館｜125社5』]（式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館、2015th year 5月3日閲覧） |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月讀尊]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（大）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}別宮 |創建 = [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=月讀宮|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (Tsukiyomi-no-miya) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Nakamura Town, [[Ise City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|12=draft|12=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|12=draft|12=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|12=draft|12=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|12=draft|12=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * == Access == * Nearest Train Station: ** Approximately 10 minutes on foot south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|ja|五十鈴川駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Toba Line|ja|近鉄鳥羽線|12=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Nearest Bus Stop: ** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通|12=draft|12=draft}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line). * Nearest Expressway Interchange: ** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Main Roads: ** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=draft|12=draft}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|12=draft|12=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side. ** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side. == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） == See Also == 社殿（2015th year ） |名称 = 月讀宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]中村町742-1[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area09.php 『式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館｜125社5』]（式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館、2015th year 5月3日閲覧） |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月讀尊]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（大）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}別宮 |創建 = [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=月讀宮|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (Tsukiyomi-no-miya) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Nakamura Town, [[Ise City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|12=draft|12=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|12=draft|12=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|12=draft|12=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|12=draft|12=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|12=draft|12=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}別宮 |創建 = [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=月讀宮|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (Tsukiyomi-no-miya) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Nakamura Town, [[Ise City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|12=draft|12=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|12=draft|12=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|12=draft|12=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|12=draft|12=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|12=draft|12=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill||Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill||Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill||Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill||Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft|12=draft}} It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|12=draft|12=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|12=draft|12=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|12=draft|12=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|12=draft|12=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|12=draft|12=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill||Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill||Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill||Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill||Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * == Access == * Nearest Train Station: ** Approximately 10 minutes on foot south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|ja|五十鈴川駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Toba Line|ja|近鉄鳥羽線|12=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Nearest Bus Stop: ** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通|12=draft|12=draft}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line). * Nearest Expressway Interchange: ** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Main Roads: ** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=draft|12=draft}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|12=draft|12=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side. ** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side. == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） == See Also == Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft|12=draft}} * [[Ise, Mie]] {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:11]] Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|12=draft|12=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|12=draft|12=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill||Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill||Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill||Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill||Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|12=draft|12=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * == Access == * Nearest Train Station: ** Approximately 10 minutes on foot south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|ja|五十鈴川駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Toba Line|ja|Toba Line|12=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Nearest Bus Stop: ** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通|12=draft|12=draft}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line). * Nearest Expressway Interchange: ** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Main Roads: ** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=draft|12=draft}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|12=draft|12=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side. ** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side. == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） == See Also == {{Commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Naiku)}} * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ise Grand Shrine]] * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft|12=draft}} * [[Ise, Mie]] {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] {{distinguish|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|8=ja|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|12=draft|12=draft}}}} {{混同|月夜見宮|8=ja|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|klt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)}} {{神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tsukiyomi no miya , 月讀宮 - panoramio (5).jpg|270px]]
社殿（2015th year ） |名称 = 月讀宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[Ise, Mie]]中村町742-1[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area09.php 『式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館｜125社5』]（式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館、2015th year 5月3日閲覧） |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月讀尊]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（大）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}別宮 |創建 = [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=月讀宮|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (Tsukiyomi-no-miya) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Nakamura Town, [[Ise City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|12=draft|12=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|12=draft|12=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|12=draft|12=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|12=draft|12=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|12=draft|12=draft}} also formed a single complex.
