Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * == Access == * Nearest Train Station: ** Approximately 10 minutes on foot south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|ja|五十鈴川駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Toba Line|ja|Toba Line|12=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|12=draft|12=draft}} operated by {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Nearest Bus Stop: ** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通|12=draft|12=draft}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line). * Nearest Expressway Interchange: ** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. * Main Roads: ** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=draft|12=draft}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|12=draft|12=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side. ** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side. == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） {{distinguish|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|8=ja|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|12=draft|12=draft}}}} {{混同|月夜見宮|8=ja|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|klt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)}} {{神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tsukiyomi no miya , 月讀宮 - panoramio (5).jpg|270px]]
社殿（2015th year ） |名称 = 月讀宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[Ise, Mie]]中村町742-1[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area09.php 『式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館｜125社5』]（式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館、2015th year 5月3日閲覧） |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月讀尊]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（大）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}別宮 |創建 = [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=月讀宮|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (Tsukiyomi-no-miya) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Nakamura Town, [[Ise City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|12=draft|12=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|12=draft|12=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|12=draft|12=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|12=draft|12=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|12=draft|12=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|12=draft|12=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|12=draft|12=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side. ** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side. == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） 社殿（2015th year ） |名称 = 月讀宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[Ise, Mie]]中村町742-1[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area09.php 『式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館｜125社5』]（式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館、2015th year 5月3日閲覧） |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月讀尊]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（大）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}別宮 |創建 = [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=月讀宮|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (Tsukiyomi-no-miya) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Nakamura Town, [[Ise City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * == Access == * Nearest Train Station: ** Approximately 10 minutes on foot south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|ja|五十鈴川駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Toba Line|ja|Toba Line|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Nearest Bus Stop: ** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line). * Nearest Expressway Interchange: ** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Main Roads: ** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side. ** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side. == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''月讀宮'''（つきよみのみや）は、[[三重県]][[伊勢市]]中村町にある[[神社]]。[[伊勢神宮]][[皇大神宮]]（内宮）別宮。[[式内社]]。「月'''読'''宮」と略字表記される場合がある。 第62回[[神宮式年遷宮]]では、内宮の遷御の約1年後の[[2014年]]（[[平成]]26年）[[10月6日]]午後8時に[[遷御]]が行われた{{Cite web|和書|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「神業?」何度も台風の直撃を回避する伊勢神宮の「遷御の儀」|publisher=[[伊勢志摩経済新聞]]|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}。 == 概要 == [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|表参道口の鳥居]] [[Image:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|内宮末社の[[葭原神社]]]] [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|手水舍と宿衛屋]] 月讀宮は[[豊受大神宮]]（外宮）から約3.8km、[[皇大神宮]]（内宮）から約1.8kmの[[五十鈴川]]中流域の中村町にある内宮別宮である。祭神は[[ツクヨミ|月讀尊]]（つきよみのみこと）。'''「つきよみさん」'''とも呼ばれるが、同じく「つきよみさん」と呼ばれる外宮別宮の[[月夜見宮]]の祭神「月夜見尊」は本別宮と同じ神とされている。 宮域には同じく内宮別宮の、月讀尊の魂を祭神とする'''月讀荒御魂宮'''（つきよみのあらみたまのみや）、[[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]]（いざなぎのみこと）を祭神とする'''伊佐奈岐宮'''（いざなぎのみや）、[[イザナミ|伊弉冉尊]]（いざなみのみこと）を祭神とする'''伊佐奈弥宮'''（いざなみのみや）の3社がある。複数の社殿が並ぶ別宮は月讀宮以外では[[瀧原宮]]の2社のみで、社殿は[[荒祭宮]]以外の内宮の他の別宮と同等で、正宮に比べれば小規模であるものの、[[神明造]]の[[社殿]]が4つ並ぶ様は壮観である。月讀荒御魂宮は2014年（平成26年）10月6日午後10時、伊佐奈岐宮・伊佐奈弥宮は[[10月10日]]に遷御を催行した。2014年（平成26年）に解体された月讀荒御魂宮の古材は、[[2012年]]（平成24年）に火災で本殿を焼失した[[栃木県]][[足利市]]緑町の[[八雲神社 (足利市)|八雲神社]]へ譲られた{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}}。 向かって右（東）から月讀荒御魂宮、月讀宮、伊佐奈岐宮、伊佐奈弥宮と並んでいるが、参拝は月讀宮-月讀荒御魂宮-伊佐奈岐宮-伊佐奈弥宮の順が正しいとされる。 最高神[[アマテラス|天照大神]]（あまてらすおおみかみ）の弟神の月讀尊が祭神であることから、内宮別宮としては天照大神の魂を祭神とする'''荒祭宮'''（あらまつりのみや）に次ぐ順位で、内宮宮域外の別宮としては最高位の別宮である。 宮域には上記別宮4社のほかに、内宮末社の'''[[葭原神社]]'''（あしはらじんじゃ）がある。ほかの境外別宮と同様に、神職が参拝時間内に常駐する宿衛屋（しゅくえいや）があり、お札・お守りの授与や、神楽や御饌の取次ぎを行なっている。 == 祭神 == * [[ツクヨミ|月讀尊]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}}（つきよみのみこと） == 歴史 == 由緒は定かではないが、第50代[[桓武天皇]]の[[延暦]]23年（[[804年]]）の'''大神宮儀式帳'''に「月讀宮一院、正殿四区」で、一囲の瑞垣内に祀られていたと記されており、別宮4社あわせて「月讀宮」と呼ばれていた。第56代[[清和天皇]]の[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]9年（[[867年]]）8月に伊佐奈岐宮と伊佐奈弥宮の宮号が与えられた。 第60代[[醍醐天皇]]の[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）の[[延喜式]]によれば、この時代には伊佐奈岐宮と伊佐奈弥宮に瑞垣をめぐらし一院とし、月讀宮と月讀荒御魂宮が同様に一院となっていたとされる。[[1873年]]（[[明治]]6年）より、4社とも個別の瑞垣を持つ現在の形になった。 == 祭事 == 皇大神宮に準じた祭事が行なわれ、祈年、月次、神嘗、新嘗の諸祭には皇室からの幣帛（へいはく）がある。 * 1月 ** 歳旦祭（さいたんさい）（1月1日） 新年を祝い、皇位の無窮を祈る祭り。 ** [[元始祭]]（げんしさい）（1月3日） 年始にあたり、天津日嗣（あまつひつぎ）の本始を祝う祭り。 * 2月 ** 建国記念祭（けんこくきねんさい）（2月11日） [[神武天皇]]の建国の創祀を祝う祭り。 ** [[祈年祭]]（きねんさい）（2月18日） 年の初めに穀物の豊穣と国家の安泰を祈る祭り。 ** 天長祭（てんちょうさい）（2月23日）[[徳仁天皇]]の誕生日を祝う祭り。 * 5月 ** 風日祈祭（かざひのみさい）（5月14日） 外宮内宮のほか、別宮末社摂社などに幣帛を供進し、風雨の災いなく五穀豊穣であるように祈る神事。 * 6月 ** 月次祭（つきなみさい）（6月18-19日） 6月と12月の11日に国家の平安と天皇の福寿を祈った祭り。神宮では神嘗祭と合わせて三節祭または三時祭と呼ぶ。 * 8月 ** 風日祈祭（かざひのみさい）（8月4日） 外宮内宮のほか、別宮末社摂社などに幣帛を供進し、風雨の災いなく五穀豊穣であるように祈る神事。 * 10月 ** [[神嘗祭]]（かんなめさい）（10月18-19日） 神官がその年に収穫された穀物を「[[神饌|大御饌（おおみけ）]]」として奉献する祭り。 * 11月 ** [[新嘗祭]]（にいなめさい）（11月24日） 天皇がその年に収穫された穀物を神に供えるとともに自らも食し、収穫を感謝する祭り。 * 12月 ** 月次祭（つきなみさい）（12月18-19日） == 境内 == [[Image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|伊佐奈岐宮と伊佐奈弥宮]] 別宮4社の社殿はほぼ同じで、祭神が男神か女神かに関係なく内宮に準じ、[[千木・鰹木|内削ぎの千木と、6本で偶数の鰹木]]を持つ萱葺の神明造で南面している。遷宮のための古殿地は通常は東西に隣接するが、月讀宮は南北であり隣接していない。月讀宮の社殿はほかの3社より若干大きく、鳥居も大きい。 * 月讀宮 - [[伊勢神宮]][[皇大神宮]]（内宮）別宮。内宮宮域外の別宮としては最高位の別宮。 * 月讀荒御魂宮 - 祭神：月讀尊荒御魂（つきよみのみことのあらみたま）。皇大神宮（内宮）別宮。 * 伊佐奈岐宮 - 祭神：[[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]]。皇大神宮（内宮）別宮。 * 伊佐奈弥宮 - 祭神：[[イザナミ|伊弉冉尊]]。皇大神宮（内宮）別宮。 * [[葭原神社]] - 祭神：佐佐津比古命（ささつひこのみこと）、[[ウカノミタマ|宇加乃御玉御祖命]]（うかのみたまのみおやのみこと）、伊加利比売命（いかりひめのみこと）。祭神はいずれも田畑を守護する五穀の神とされる。皇大神宮（内宮）末社。葭原神社は内宮に準じ、内削ぎの千木と偶数の4本の鰹木に板葺の神明造である。 * 宿衛屋 == 交通 == * 最寄駅：[[近畿日本鉄道|近鉄]][[近鉄鳥羽線|鳥羽線]][[五十鈴川駅]]から南へ徒歩約10分 ::[[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[参宮線]][[伊勢市駅]]から徒歩約1時間 * 最寄バス停：[[三重交通]][[三重交通伊勢営業所|51系統・外宮内宮線]]、中村町バス停下車徒歩約5分 * 最寄インターチェンジ：[[伊勢自動車道]][[伊勢インターチェンジ]]から約1km * 一般道路：[[三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線]]（[[御幸道路]]）沿い（表参道口）、[[国道23号]]沿い（裏参道口） * 駐車場：国道側にバスも置ける大きな駐車場があるが、県道側にも数台駐車できる。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） == 関連項目 == {{Commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Naiku)}} * [[ツクヨミ]] * [[伊勢神宮]] * [[神宮125社の一覧]] * [[伊勢市]] {{神宮125社}} {{神道 横}} {{デフォルトソート:つきよみのみや}} [[Category:神宮125社]] [[Category:式内大社]] 最寄駅：[[近畿日本鉄道|近鉄]][[近鉄鳥羽線|鳥羽線]][[五十鈴川駅]]から南へ徒歩約10分 ::[[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[参宮線]][[伊勢市駅]]から徒歩約1時間 * 最寄バス停：[[三重交通]][[三重交通伊勢営業所|51系統・外宮内宮線]]、中村町バス停下車徒歩約5分 * 最寄インターチェンジ：[[伊勢自動車道]][[伊勢インターチェンジ]]から約1km * 社殿（2015th year ） |名称 = 月讀宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[Ise, Mie]]中村町742-1[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area09.php 『式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館｜125社5』]（式年遷宮記念 せんぐう館、2015th year 5月3日閲覧） |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月讀尊]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（大）
{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}別宮 |創建 = [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=月讀宮|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (Tsukiyomi-no-miya) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Nakamura Town, [[Ise City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == [[image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Izanagi-no-Miya and Izanami-no-Miya]] The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * == Access == * Nearest Train Station: ** Approximately 10 minutes on foot south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|ja|五十鈴川駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Toba Line|ja|Toba Line|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Nearest Bus Stop: ** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line). * Nearest Expressway Interchange: ** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Main Roads: ** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side. ** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side. == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity. Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * Line|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Nearest Bus Stop: ** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line). * Nearest Expressway Interchange: ** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Main Roads: ** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines: * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto) * '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto) Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shimmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014. The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga)|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}} From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank. Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋|qq=draft|qq=draft}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings. == {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}} == History == The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were officially granted their shrine titles. According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Daigo|ja|醍醐天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} also formed a single complex. Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure. == Festivals == Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai. * January ** {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Saiten-sai}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne. ** {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji). * February ** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan. ** {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation. ** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * May ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest. * June ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine. * August ** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity. * October ** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty. * November ** {{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest. * December ** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|en:draft|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Inner Shrine). ** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=月讀荒御魂宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi. ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈岐宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt_ja=伊佐奈弥宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto). ** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ** Enshrined Deities: - Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命) - Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命) - Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命) ** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops. ** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine. ** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing. * Shukueiya (宿衛屋) ** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances. * * * * == Access == * Nearest Train Station: ** Approximately 10 minutes on foot south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|ja|五十鈴川駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Toba Line|ja|Toba Line|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. ** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Ise-shi Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|JR Sangū Line|ja|参宮線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} operated by {{ill|JR Central|ja|東海旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Nearest Bus Stop: ** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line). * Nearest Expressway Interchange: ** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|ja|伊勢自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * Main Roads: ** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance. ** Accessible via {{ill|National Route 23 (Japan)|ja|国道23号|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the rear approach entrance. * Parking: ** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side. ** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side. == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 『月讀宮以下四別宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） == See Also == {{Commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Naiku)}} * [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ise Grand Shrine]] * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * [[Ise, Mie]] {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{translated page|ja|月讀宮|version=99561516|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}別宮 |創建 = [[延暦]]23rd year （[[804]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=月讀宮|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (Tsukiyomi-no-miya) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Nakamura Town, [[Ise City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮." During the 62nd [[Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengu|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on [[October 6]], [[2014]] ({{ill|Heisei era|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26) at 8:00 PM.{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=「Divine Work?」 The "Sengu no Gi" of Ise Jingū Avoids Multiple Direct Typhoon Hits|publisher={{ill|Ise-Shima Economic Newspaper|ja|伊勢志摩経済新聞|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. == Overview == [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]] [[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Betsugu|ja|別宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity.
