{{jalink|Kōtaijingū|Q11581011}} Auxiliary Shrine |Established = Before {{jalink|Enryaku|Q1373176}} 23 ({{jalink|804|Q29998}}) |Main hall style = {{jalink|Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545}} |Annual festival = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-miya''' (つきよみのみや) is a Shinto shrine located in Nakamura-chō, {{jalink|Ise City|Q328067}}, {{jalink|Mie Prefecture|Q128196}}. It is an auxiliary shrine (betsugū) of {{jalink|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168}} {{jalink|Kōtaijingū|Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). It is a {{jalink|Shikinaisha}}. It is sometimes written with the abbreviated characters “月読宮”. At the 62nd {{jalink|Shikinen Sengū of Ise Grand Shrine|Q3959472}}, the transfer of the deity ({{jalink|Sengu|Q24892914}}) was performed at 8:00 p.m. on {{jalink|October 6|Q2928}}, {{jalink|2014|Q1999}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}} 26), about one year after the transfer at the Inner Shrine{{Cite web|ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=“‘Divine works?’ Ise Grand Shrine’s ‘Sengu ceremony’ repeatedly avoids direct typhoon hits”|publisher={{jalink|Ise-Shima Keizai Shimbun|Q18700592}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. === Enshrined deities === {{jalink|Tsukuyomi|Q595520|'''Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto'''}}{{Cite web |url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/ |title=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Auxiliary Shrine of the Inner Shrine) |accessdate=2024-03-09}} (つきよみのみこと) – the second worship hall from the right when facing Tsukiyomi-no-miya. '''{{jalink|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama}}''' – the rightmost worship hall when facing Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya. '''{{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}''' – the third worship hall from the right when facing Isanagi-no-miya. '''{{jalink|Izanami|Q682306|Izanami-no-Mikoto}}''' – the leftmost worship hall when facing Isanami-no-miya. === Overview === [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the main approach entrance]] [[Image:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{jalink|Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305}}, a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Temizuya and guardhouse]] Tsukiyomi-no-miya is an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine located in Nakamura-chō along the middle reaches of the {{jalink|Isuzu River|Q6089522}}, about 3.8 km from {{jalink|Toyouke Daijingū|Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from {{jalink|Kōtaijingū|Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). The enshrined deity is {{jalink|Tsukuyomi|Q595520|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. It is also affectionately called “Tsukiyomi-san”; however, the enshrined deity “Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto” of {{jalink|Tsukiyo-mi-no-miya|Q11516023}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine also called “Tsukiyomi-san,” is considered the same deity as that of the main auxiliary shrine. Within the precincts are three other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine: '''Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya''', which enshrines the aramitama (rough spirit) of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto; '''Isanagi-no-miya''', which enshrines {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; and '''Isanami-no-miya''', which enshrines {{jalink|Izanami|Q682306|Izanami-no-Mikoto}}. Aside from Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings lined up is {{jalink|Takihara-no-miya|Q11566292}}, which has two. The shrine buildings are comparable in scale to other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine except {{jalink|Aramatsuri-no-miya|Q2859485}}; though smaller than the main sanctuary, the sight of four {{jalink|Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545}} shrine buildings standing in a row is magnificent. The transfer ceremonies were held for Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya at 10:00 p.m. on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya on {{jalink|October 10|Q2921}}. Old timbers from Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, dismantled in 2014, were donated to {{jalink|Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga City)|Q11391850|Yakumo Shrine}} in Midori-chō, {{jalink|Ashikaga City|Q374477}}, {{jalink|Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843}}, which lost its main hall to a fire in {{jalink|2012|Q1990}} (Heisei 24){{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=“Long-awaited main hall at Yakumo Shrine—donated by Ise Grand Shrine”|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}}. From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, Tsukiyomi-no-miya, Isanagi-no-miya, and Isanami-no-miya; however, the correct order of worship is said to be Tsukiyomi-no-miya → Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya → Isanagi-no-miya → Isanami-no-miya. Because Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the younger sibling deity of the supreme deity {{jalink|Amaterasu||Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, is enshrined here, Tsukiyomi-no-miya ranks second among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine after '''Aramatsuri-no-miya''', which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, and it is the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine’s main precinct. In addition to the four auxiliary shrines above, the precincts include '''{{jalink|Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305}}''', a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. As with other off-site auxiliary shrines, there is a guardhouse (shukueiya) staffed by priests during visiting hours, where talismans and amulets are bestowed and arrangements are made for kagura dances and food offerings. === History === Although the exact origins are unclear, the “Daijingū Gishikichō” records that in {{jalink|Enryaku|Q1373176}} 23 ({{jalink|804|Q29998}}) during the reign of the 50th emperor {{jalink|Emperor Kanmu|Q314846}}, “Tsukiyomi-no-miya, one compound, four main sanctuaries” were enshrined within a single sacred fence, and the four auxiliary shrines together were called “Tsukiyomi-no-miya.” In {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōgan}} 9 ({{jalink|867|Q30347}}) during the reign of the 56th emperor {{jalink|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243}}, the shrine names Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya were granted. According to the {{jalink|Engishiki|Q1342448}} of {{jalink|Enchō|Q1327274|Enchō}} 5 ({{jalink|927|Q30470}}) during the reign of the 60th emperor {{jalink|Emperor Daigo|Q329753}}, at that time Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya formed one compound enclosed by a sacred fence, and likewise Tsukiyomi-no-miya and Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya formed another. From {{jalink|1873|Q7757}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}} 6), all four shrines came to have their own individual sacred fences, forming the current layout. === Festivals === Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of the Inner Shrine, and for major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai, offerings (heihaku) are presented from the Imperial Household. * January ** Saitansai (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial line. ** {{jalink|Genshisai|Q11387821}} (January 3): A festival celebrating the origin of the imperial succession at the start of the year. * February ** National Foundation Commemoration Festival (February 11): A festival celebrating the founding of the nation by {{jalink|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188}}. ** {{jalink|Kinensai|Q118906710}} (February 18): A festival praying for a bountiful harvest and national peace at the beginning of the year. ** Tenchōsai (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{jalink|Emperor Naruhito}}. * May ** Kazahinomisai (May 14): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * June ** Tsukinamisai (June 18–19): A festival held in June and December praying for national peace and the emperor’s well-being; at Ise Grand Shrine it is, together with the Kannamesai, called one of the Three Seasonal Festivals. * August ** Kazahinomisai (August 4): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * October ** {{jalink|Kannamesai|Q11255045}} (October 18–19): A festival in which priests offer newly harvested grain of the year as sacred food ({{jalink|Shinsen|Q11591045|Ōmike}}). * November ** {{jalink|Niinamesai|Q11501518}} (November 24): A festival in which the emperor offers newly harvested grain to the deities and partakes of it himself, giving thanks for the harvest. * December ** Tsukinamisai (December 18–19) === Precincts === [[Image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya]] The shrine buildings of the four auxiliary shrines are nearly identical and, regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female, follow the Inner Shrine style: thatched Shinmei-zukuri facing south, with inward-cut chigi and an even number (six) of katsuogi. The old shrine sites for periodic rebuilding are usually adjacent east–west, but at Tsukiyomi-no-miya they are arranged north–south and are not adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii is also larger. * Tsukiyomi-no-miya – Auxiliary shrine of {{jalink|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168}} {{jalink|Kōtaijingū|Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine); the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine precinct. * Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya – Enshrined deity: Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanagi-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanami-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Izanami|Q682306|Izanami-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * {{jalink|Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305}} – Enshrined deities: Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto, {{jalink|Ukanomitama|Q3080728|Ukanomitama no Mionoya no Mikoto}}, and Ikarihime-no-Mikoto; all are considered deities of the five grains who protect fields and paddies. A subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. Ashihara Shrine follows the Inner Shrine style, with inward-cut chigi and four (even-numbered) katsuogi, in a board-roofed Shinmei-zukuri style. * Guardhouse === Access === * Nearest station: About a 10-minute walk south from {{jalink|Isuzugawa Station|Q6089533}} on the {{jalink|Kintetsu Toba Line|Q5357612}} of {{jalink|Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085}} :: About a 1-hour walk from {{jalink|Ise-shi Station|Q6079748}} on the {{jalink|Sangū Line|Q872023}} of {{jalink|JR Central|Q513679}} * Nearest bus stop: About a 5-minute walk from Nakamura-chō bus stop on the 51 Outer–Inner Shrine Line of {{jalink|Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516}} ({{jalink|Mie Kōtsū Ise Office|Q11357667}}) * Nearest interchange: About 1 km from {{jalink|Ise Interchange|Q10884857}} on the {{jalink|Ise Expressway|Q6079578}} * Roads: Along {{jalink|Mie Prefectural Route 37 Toba–Matsusaka Line|Q11357923}} ({{jalink|Miyuki Road|Q22222736}}) (main approach), and along {{jalink|National Route 23|Q5357579}} (rear approach) * Parking: There is a large parking lot on the national road side that can accommodate buses; several cars can also be parked on the prefectural road side. === Notes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === References === * “Guide to Visiting the Four Auxiliary Shrines Including Tsukiyomi-no-miya” (published by the Jingu Administration Office) * “Walking around Oise-san” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) * “Oise Pilgrimage” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) === See also === {{Commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Naiku)}} * {{jalink|Tsukuyomi|Q595520}} * {{jalink|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168}} * {{jalink|List of the 125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine|Q16482760}} * {{jalink|Ise City|Q328067}} {{125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine}} {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsukiyomi-no-miya}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Ronsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Subshrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:神宮125社]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社|大つきよみのみや]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:2014年竣工の日本の建築物]]

{{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} Auxiliary Shrine |Established = Before {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|lt=804|Q29998|WD=Q29998}}) |Main hall style = {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545}} |Annual festival = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-miya''' (つきよみのみや) is a Shinto shrine located in Nakamura-chō, {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|WD=Q328067}}, {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|WD=Q128196}}. It is an auxiliary shrine (betsugū) of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). It is a {{ill||lt=Shikinaisha|UNKNOWN}}. It is sometimes written with the abbreviated characters “月読宮”. At the 62nd {{ill|lt=Shikinen Sengū of Ise Grand Shrine|Q3959472|WD=Q3959472}}, the transfer of the deity ({{ill|lt=Sengu|Q24892914|WD=Q24892914}}) was performed at 8:00 p.m. on {{ill|lt=October 6|Q2928|WD=Q2928}}, {{ill|lt=2014|Q1999|WD=Q1999}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510}} 26), about one year after the transfer at the Inner Shrine{{Cite web|ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=“‘Divine works?’ Ise Grand Shrine’s ‘Sengu ceremony’ repeatedly avoids direct typhoon hits”|publisher={{ill|lt=Ise-Shima Keizai Shimbun|Q18700592|WD=Q18700592}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. === Enshrined deities === {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt='''Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto'''}}{{Cite web |url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/ |title=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Auxiliary Shrine of the Inner Shrine) |accessdate=2024-03-09}} (つきよみのみこと) – the second worship hall from the right when facing Tsukiyomi-no-miya. '''{{ill||lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama|UNKNOWN}}''' – the rightmost worship hall when facing Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya. '''{{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}''' – the third worship hall from the right when facing Isanagi-no-miya. '''{{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}''' – the leftmost worship hall when facing Isanami-no-miya. === Overview === [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the main approach entrance]] [[Image:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}}, a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Temizuya and guardhouse]] Tsukiyomi-no-miya is an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine located in Nakamura-chō along the middle reaches of the {{ill|lt=Isuzu River|Q6089522|WD=Q6089522}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|lt=Toyouke Daijingū|Q11633343|WD=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. It is also affectionately called “Tsukiyomi-san”; however, the enshrined deity “Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto” of {{ill|lt=Tsukiyo-mi-no-miya|Q11516023|WD=Q11516023}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine also called “Tsukiyomi-san,” is considered the same deity as that of the main auxiliary shrine. Within the precincts are three other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine: '''Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya''', which enshrines the aramitama (rough spirit) of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto; '''Isanagi-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; and '''Isanami-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}. Aside from Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings lined up is {{ill|lt=Takihara-no-miya|Q11566292|WD=Q11566292}}, which has two. The shrine buildings are comparable in scale to other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine except {{ill|lt=Aramatsuri-no-miya|Q2859485|WD=Q2859485}}; though smaller than the main sanctuary, the sight of four {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545}} shrine buildings standing in a row is magnificent. The transfer ceremonies were held for Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya at 10:00 p.m. on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya on {{ill|lt=October 10|Q2921|WD=Q2921}}. Old timbers from Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, dismantled in 2014, were donated to {{ill|lt=Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga City)|Q11391850|WD=Q11391850|lt=Yakumo Shrine}} in Midori-chō, {{ill|lt=Ashikaga City|Q374477|WD=Q374477}}, {{ill|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843|WD=Q44843}}, which lost its main hall to a fire in {{ill|lt=2012|Q1990|WD=Q1990}} (Heisei 24){{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=“Long-awaited main hall at Yakumo Shrine—donated by Ise Grand Shrine”|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}}. From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, Tsukiyomi-no-miya, Isanagi-no-miya, and Isanami-no-miya; however, the correct order of worship is said to be Tsukiyomi-no-miya → Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya → Isanagi-no-miya → Isanami-no-miya. Because Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the younger sibling deity of the supreme deity {{ill|lt=Amaterasu||WD=|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, is enshrined here, Tsukiyomi-no-miya ranks second among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine after '''Aramatsuri-no-miya''', which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, and it is the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine’s main precinct. In addition to the four auxiliary shrines above, the precincts include '''{{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}}''', a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. As with other off-site auxiliary shrines, there is a guardhouse (shukueiya) staffed by priests during visiting hours, where talismans and amulets are bestowed and arrangements are made for kagura dances and food offerings. === History === Although the exact origins are unclear, the “Daijingū Gishikichō” records that in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|lt=804|Q29998|WD=Q29998}}) during the reign of the 50th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Kanmu|Q314846|WD=Q314846}}, “Tsukiyomi-no-miya, one compound, four main sanctuaries” were enshrined within a single sacred fence, and the four auxiliary shrines together were called “Tsukiyomi-no-miya.” In {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 9 ({{ill|lt=867|Q30347|WD=Q30347}}) during the reign of the 56th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|WD=Q349243}}, the shrine names Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya were granted. According to the {{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448}} of {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470}}) during the reign of the 60th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Daigo|Q329753|WD=Q329753}}, at that time Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya formed one compound enclosed by a sacred fence, and likewise Tsukiyomi-no-miya and Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya formed another. From {{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|WD=Q7757}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}} 6), all four shrines came to have their own individual sacred fences, forming the current layout. === Festivals === Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of the Inner Shrine, and for major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai, offerings (heihaku) are presented from the Imperial Household. * January ** Saitansai (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial line. ** {{ill|lt=Genshisai|Q11387821|WD=Q11387821}} (January 3): A festival celebrating the origin of the imperial succession at the start of the year. * February ** National Foundation Commemoration Festival (February 11): A festival celebrating the founding of the nation by {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188}}. ** {{ill|lt=Kinensai|Q118906710|WD=Q118906710}} (February 18): A festival praying for a bountiful harvest and national peace at the beginning of the year. ** Tenchōsai (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill||lt=Emperor Naruhito|UNKNOWN}}. * May ** Kazahinomisai (May 14): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * June ** Tsukinamisai (June 18–19): A festival held in June and December praying for national peace and the emperor’s well-being; at Ise Grand Shrine it is, together with the Kannamesai, called one of the Three Seasonal Festivals. * August ** Kazahinomisai (August 4): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * October ** {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|WD=Q11255045}} (October 18–19): A festival in which priests offer newly harvested grain of the year as sacred food ({{ill|lt=Shinsen|Q11591045|WD=Q11591045|lt=Ōmike}}). * November ** {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|WD=Q11501518}} (November 24): A festival in which the emperor offers newly harvested grain to the deities and partakes of it himself, giving thanks for the harvest. * December ** Tsukinamisai (December 18–19) === Precincts === [[Image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya]] The shrine buildings of the four auxiliary shrines are nearly identical and, regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female, follow the Inner Shrine style: thatched Shinmei-zukuri facing south, with inward-cut chigi and an even number (six) of katsuogi. The old shrine sites for periodic rebuilding are usually adjacent east–west, but at Tsukiyomi-no-miya they are arranged north–south and are not adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii is also larger. * Tsukiyomi-no-miya – Auxiliary shrine of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine); the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine precinct. * Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya – Enshrined deity: Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanagi-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanami-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}} – Enshrined deities: Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto, {{ill|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama no Mionoya no Mikoto}}, and Ikarihime-no-Mikoto; all are considered deities of the five grains who protect fields and paddies. A subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. Ashihara Shrine follows the Inner Shrine style, with inward-cut chigi and four (even-numbered) katsuogi, in a board-roofed Shinmei-zukuri style. * Guardhouse === Access === * Nearest station: About a 10-minute walk south from {{ill|lt=Isuzugawa Station|Q6089533|WD=Q6089533}} on the {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Toba Line|Q5357612|WD=Q5357612}} of {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|WD=Q1531085}} :: About a 1-hour walk from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|WD=Q6079748}} on the {{ill|lt=Sangū Line|Q872023|WD=Q872023}} of {{ill|lt=JR Central|Q513679|WD=Q513679}} * Nearest bus stop: About a 5-minute walk from Nakamura-chō bus stop on the 51 Outer–Inner Shrine Line of {{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516|WD=Q6843516}} ({{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū Ise Office|Q11357667|WD=Q11357667}}) * Nearest interchange: About 1 km from {{ill|lt=Ise Interchange|Q10884857|WD=Q10884857}} on the {{ill|lt=Ise Expressway|Q6079578|WD=Q6079578}} * Roads: Along {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 37 Toba–Matsusaka Line|Q11357923|WD=Q11357923}} ({{ill|lt=Miyuki Road|Q22222736|WD=Q22222736}}) (main approach), and along {{ill|lt=National Route 23|Q5357579|WD=Q5357579}} (rear approach) * Parking: There is a large parking lot on the national road side that can accommodate buses; several cars can also be parked on the prefectural road side. === Notes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === References === * “Guide to Visiting the Four Auxiliary Shrines Including Tsukiyomi-no-miya” (published by the Jingu Administration Office) * “Walking around Oise-san” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) * “Oise Pilgrimage” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) === See also === {{Commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Naiku)}} * {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520}} * {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} * {{ill|lt=List of the 125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine|Q16482760|WD=Q16482760}} * {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|WD=Q328067}} {{125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine}} {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsukiyomi-no-miya}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Ronsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Subshrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:神宮125社]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社|大つきよみのみや]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:2014年竣工の日本の建築物]]

{{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} Auxiliary Shrine |Established = Before {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|lt=804|Q29998|WD=Q29998}}) |Main hall style = {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545}} |Annual festival = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-miya''' (つきよみのみや) is a Shinto shrine located in Nakamura-chō, {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|WD=Q328067}}, {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|WD=Q128196}}. It is an auxiliary shrine (betsugū) of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|UNKNOWN}}. It is sometimes written with the abbreviated characters “月読宮”. At the 62nd {{ill|lt=Shikinen Sengū of Ise Grand Shrine|Q3959472|WD=Q3959472}}, the transfer of the deity ({{ill|lt=Sengu|Q24892914|WD=Q24892914}}) was performed at 8:00 p.m. on {{ill|lt=October 6|Q2928|WD=Q2928}}, {{ill|lt=2014|Q1999|WD=Q1999}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510}} 26), about one year after the transfer at the Inner Shrine{{Cite web|ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=“‘Divine works?’ Ise Grand Shrine’s ‘Sengu ceremony’ repeatedly avoids direct typhoon hits”|publisher={{ill|lt=Ise-Shima Keizai Shimbun|Q18700592|WD=Q18700592}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. === Enshrined deities === {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt='''Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto'''}}{{Cite web |url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/ |title=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Auxiliary Shrine of the Inner Shrine) |accessdate=2024-03-09}} (つきよみのみこと) – the second worship hall from the right when facing Tsukiyomi-no-miya. '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama|UNKNOWN}}''' – the rightmost worship hall when facing Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya. '''{{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}''' – the third worship hall from the right when facing Isanagi-no-miya. '''{{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}''' – the leftmost worship hall when facing Isanami-no-miya. === Overview === [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the main approach entrance]] [[Image:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}}, a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Temizuya and guardhouse]] Tsukiyomi-no-miya is an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine located in Nakamura-chō along the middle reaches of the {{ill|lt=Isuzu River|Q6089522|WD=Q6089522}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|lt=Toyouke Daijingū|Q11633343|WD=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. It is also affectionately called “Tsukiyomi-san”; however, the enshrined deity “Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto” of {{ill|lt=Tsukiyo-mi-no-miya|Q11516023|WD=Q11516023}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine also called “Tsukiyomi-san,” is considered the same deity as that of the main auxiliary shrine. Within the precincts are three other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine: '''Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya''', which enshrines the aramitama (rough spirit) of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto; '''Isanagi-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; and '''Isanami-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}. Aside from Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings lined up is {{ill|lt=Takihara-no-miya|Q11566292|WD=Q11566292}}, which has two. The shrine buildings are comparable in scale to other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine except {{ill|lt=Aramatsuri-no-miya|Q2859485|WD=Q2859485}}; though smaller than the main sanctuary, the sight of four {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545}} shrine buildings standing in a row is magnificent. The transfer ceremonies were held for Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya at 10:00 p.m. on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya on {{ill|lt=October 10|Q2921|WD=Q2921}}. Old timbers from Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, dismantled in 2014, were donated to {{ill|lt=Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga City)|Q11391850|WD=Q11391850|lt=Yakumo Shrine}} in Midori-chō, {{ill|lt=Ashikaga City|Q374477|WD=Q374477}}, {{ill|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843|WD=Q44843}}, which lost its main hall to a fire in {{ill|lt=2012|Q1990|WD=Q1990}} (Heisei 24){{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=“Long-awaited main hall at Yakumo Shrine—donated by Ise Grand Shrine”|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}}. From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, Tsukiyomi-no-miya, Isanagi-no-miya, and Isanami-no-miya; however, the correct order of worship is said to be Tsukiyomi-no-miya → Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya → Isanagi-no-miya → Isanami-no-miya. Because Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the younger sibling deity of the supreme deity {{ill|lt=Amaterasu||WD=|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, is enshrined here, Tsukiyomi-no-miya ranks second among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine after '''Aramatsuri-no-miya''', which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, and it is the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine’s main precinct. In addition to the four auxiliary shrines above, the precincts include '''{{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}}''', a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. As with other off-site auxiliary shrines, there is a guardhouse (shukueiya) staffed by priests during visiting hours, where talismans and amulets are bestowed and arrangements are made for kagura dances and food offerings. === History === Although the exact origins are unclear, the “Daijingū Gishikichō” records that in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|lt=804|Q29998|WD=Q29998}}) during the reign of the 50th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Kanmu|Q314846|WD=Q314846}}, “Tsukiyomi-no-miya, one compound, four main sanctuaries” were enshrined within a single sacred fence, and the four auxiliary shrines together were called “Tsukiyomi-no-miya.” In {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 9 ({{ill|lt=867|Q30347|WD=Q30347}}) during the reign of the 56th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|WD=Q349243}}, the shrine names Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya were granted. According to the {{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448}} of {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470}}) during the reign of the 60th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Daigo|Q329753|WD=Q329753}}, at that time Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya formed one compound enclosed by a sacred fence, and likewise Tsukiyomi-no-miya and Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya formed another. From {{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|WD=Q7757}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}} 6), all four shrines came to have their own individual sacred fences, forming the current layout. === Festivals === Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of the Inner Shrine, and for major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai, offerings (heihaku) are presented from the Imperial Household. * January ** Saitansai (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial line. ** {{ill|lt=Genshisai|Q11387821|WD=Q11387821}} (January 3): A festival celebrating the origin of the imperial succession at the start of the year. * February ** National Foundation Commemoration Festival (February 11): A festival celebrating the founding of the nation by {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188}}. ** {{ill|lt=Kinensai|Q118906710|WD=Q118906710}} (February 18): A festival praying for a bountiful harvest and national peace at the beginning of the year. ** Tenchōsai (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Naruhito|UNKNOWN}}. * May ** Kazahinomisai (May 14): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * June ** Tsukinamisai (June 18–19): A festival held in June and December praying for national peace and the emperor’s well-being; at Ise Grand Shrine it is, together with the Kannamesai, called one of the Three Seasonal Festivals. * August ** Kazahinomisai (August 4): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * October ** {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|WD=Q11255045}} (October 18–19): A festival in which priests offer newly harvested grain of the year as sacred food ({{ill|lt=Shinsen|Q11591045|WD=Q11591045|lt=Ōmike}}). * November ** {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|WD=Q11501518}} (November 24): A festival in which the emperor offers newly harvested grain to the deities and partakes of it himself, giving thanks for the harvest. * December ** Tsukinamisai (December 18–19) === Precincts === [[Image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya]] The shrine buildings of the four auxiliary shrines are nearly identical and, regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female, follow the Inner Shrine style: thatched Shinmei-zukuri facing south, with inward-cut chigi and an even number (six) of katsuogi. The old shrine sites for periodic rebuilding are usually adjacent east–west, but at Tsukiyomi-no-miya they are arranged north–south and are not adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii is also larger. * Tsukiyomi-no-miya – Auxiliary shrine of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine); the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine precinct. * Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya – Enshrined deity: Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanagi-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanami-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}} – Enshrined deities: Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto, {{ill|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama no Mionoya no Mikoto}}, and Ikarihime-no-Mikoto; all are considered deities of the five grains who protect fields and paddies. A subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. Ashihara Shrine follows the Inner Shrine style, with inward-cut chigi and four (even-numbered) katsuogi, in a board-roofed Shinmei-zukuri style. * Guardhouse === Access === * Nearest station: About a 10-minute walk south from {{ill|lt=Isuzugawa Station|Q6089533|WD=Q6089533}} on the {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Toba Line|Q5357612|WD=Q5357612}} of {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|WD=Q1531085}} :: About a 1-hour walk from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|WD=Q6079748}} on the {{ill|lt=Sangū Line|Q872023|WD=Q872023}} of {{ill|lt=JR Central|Q513679|WD=Q513679}} * Nearest bus stop: About a 5-minute walk from Nakamura-chō bus stop on the 51 Outer–Inner Shrine Line of {{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516|WD=Q6843516}} ({{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū Ise Office|Q11357667|WD=Q11357667}}) * Nearest interchange: About 1 km from {{ill|lt=Ise Interchange|Q10884857|WD=Q10884857}} on the {{ill|lt=Ise Expressway|Q6079578|WD=Q6079578}} * Roads: Along {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 37 Toba–Matsusaka Line|Q11357923|WD=Q11357923}} ({{ill|lt=Miyuki Road|Q22222736|WD=Q22222736}}) (main approach), and along {{ill|lt=National Route 23|Q5357579|WD=Q5357579}} (rear approach) * Parking: There is a large parking lot on the national road side that can accommodate buses; several cars can also be parked on the prefectural road side. === Notes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === References === * “Guide to Visiting the Four Auxiliary Shrines Including Tsukiyomi-no-miya” (published by the Jingu Administration Office) * “Walking around Oise-san” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) * “Oise Pilgrimage” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) === See also === {{Commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Naiku)}} * {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520}} * {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} * {{ill|lt=List of the 125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine|Q16482760|WD=Q16482760}} * {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|WD=Q328067}} {{125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine}} {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsukiyomi-no-miya}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Ronsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Subshrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:神宮125社]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社|大つきよみのみや]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:2014年竣工の日本の建築物]]

{{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} Auxiliary Shrine |Established = Before {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|lt=804|Q29998|WD=Q29998}}) |Main hall style = {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545}} |Annual festival = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-miya''' (つきよみのみや) is a Shinto shrine located in Nakamura-chō, {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|WD=Q328067}}, {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|WD=Q128196}}. It is an auxiliary shrine (betsugū) of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=UNKNOWN}}. It is sometimes written with the abbreviated characters “月読宮”. At the 62nd {{ill|lt=Shikinen Sengū of Ise Grand Shrine|Q3959472|WD=Q3959472}}, the transfer of the deity ({{ill|lt=Sengu|Q24892914|WD=Q24892914}}) was performed at 8:00 p.m. on {{ill|lt=October 6|Q2928|WD=Q2928}}, {{ill|lt=2014|Q1999|WD=Q1999}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510}} 26), about one year after the transfer at the Inner Shrine{{Cite web|ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=“‘Divine works?’ Ise Grand Shrine’s ‘Sengu ceremony’ repeatedly avoids direct typhoon hits”|publisher={{ill|lt=Ise-Shima Keizai Shimbun|Q18700592|WD=Q18700592}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. === Enshrined deities === {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt='''Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto'''}}{{Cite web |url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/ |title=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Auxiliary Shrine of the Inner Shrine) |accessdate=2024-03-09}} (つきよみのみこと) – the second worship hall from the right when facing Tsukiyomi-no-miya. '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama|1=UNKNOWN}}''' – the rightmost worship hall when facing Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya. '''{{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}''' – the third worship hall from the right when facing Isanagi-no-miya. '''{{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}''' – the leftmost worship hall when facing Isanami-no-miya. === Overview === [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the main approach entrance]] [[Image:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}}, a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Temizuya and guardhouse]] Tsukiyomi-no-miya is an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine located in Nakamura-chō along the middle reaches of the {{ill|lt=Isuzu River|Q6089522|WD=Q6089522}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|lt=Toyouke Daijingū|Q11633343|WD=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. It is also affectionately called “Tsukiyomi-san”; however, the enshrined deity “Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto” of {{ill|lt=Tsukiyo-mi-no-miya|Q11516023|WD=Q11516023}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine also called “Tsukiyomi-san,” is considered the same deity as that of the main auxiliary shrine. Within the precincts are three other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine: '''Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya''', which enshrines the aramitama (rough spirit) of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto; '''Isanagi-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; and '''Isanami-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}. Aside from Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings lined up is {{ill|lt=Takihara-no-miya|Q11566292|WD=Q11566292}}, which has two. The shrine buildings are comparable in scale to other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine except {{ill|lt=Aramatsuri-no-miya|Q2859485|WD=Q2859485}}; though smaller than the main sanctuary, the sight of four {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545}} shrine buildings standing in a row is magnificent. The transfer ceremonies were held for Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya at 10:00 p.m. on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya on {{ill|lt=October 10|Q2921|WD=Q2921}}. Old timbers from Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, dismantled in 2014, were donated to {{ill|lt=Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga City)|Q11391850|WD=Q11391850|lt=Yakumo Shrine}} in Midori-chō, {{ill|lt=Ashikaga City|Q374477|WD=Q374477}}, {{ill|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843|WD=Q44843}}, which lost its main hall to a fire in {{ill|lt=2012|Q1990|WD=Q1990}} (Heisei 24){{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=“Long-awaited main hall at Yakumo Shrine—donated by Ise Grand Shrine”|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}}. From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, Tsukiyomi-no-miya, Isanagi-no-miya, and Isanami-no-miya; however, the correct order of worship is said to be Tsukiyomi-no-miya → Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya → Isanagi-no-miya → Isanami-no-miya. Because Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the younger sibling deity of the supreme deity {{ill|lt=Amaterasu||WD=|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, is enshrined here, Tsukiyomi-no-miya ranks second among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine after '''Aramatsuri-no-miya''', which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, and it is the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine’s main precinct. In addition to the four auxiliary shrines above, the precincts include '''{{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}}''', a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. As with other off-site auxiliary shrines, there is a guardhouse (shukueiya) staffed by priests during visiting hours, where talismans and amulets are bestowed and arrangements are made for kagura dances and food offerings. === History === Although the exact origins are unclear, the “Daijingū Gishikichō” records that in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|lt=804|Q29998|WD=Q29998}}) during the reign of the 50th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Kanmu|Q314846|WD=Q314846}}, “Tsukiyomi-no-miya, one compound, four main sanctuaries” were enshrined within a single sacred fence, and the four auxiliary shrines together were called “Tsukiyomi-no-miya.” In {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 9 ({{ill|lt=867|Q30347|WD=Q30347}}) during the reign of the 56th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|WD=Q349243}}, the shrine names Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya were granted. According to the {{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448}} of {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470}}) during the reign of the 60th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Daigo|Q329753|WD=Q329753}}, at that time Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya formed one compound enclosed by a sacred fence, and likewise Tsukiyomi-no-miya and Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya formed another. From {{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|WD=Q7757}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}} 6), all four shrines came to have their own individual sacred fences, forming the current layout. === Festivals === Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of the Inner Shrine, and for major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai, offerings (heihaku) are presented from the Imperial Household. * January ** Saitansai (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial line. ** {{ill|lt=Genshisai|Q11387821|WD=Q11387821}} (January 3): A festival celebrating the origin of the imperial succession at the start of the year. * February ** National Foundation Commemoration Festival (February 11): A festival celebrating the founding of the nation by {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188}}. ** {{ill|lt=Kinensai|Q118906710|WD=Q118906710}} (February 18): A festival praying for a bountiful harvest and national peace at the beginning of the year. ** Tenchōsai (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Naruhito|1=UNKNOWN}}. * May ** Kazahinomisai (May 14): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * June ** Tsukinamisai (June 18–19): A festival held in June and December praying for national peace and the emperor’s well-being; at Ise Grand Shrine it is, together with the Kannamesai, called one of the Three Seasonal Festivals. * August ** Kazahinomisai (August 4): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * October ** {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|WD=Q11255045}} (October 18–19): A festival in which priests offer newly harvested grain of the year as sacred food ({{ill|lt=Shinsen|Q11591045|WD=Q11591045|lt=Ōmike}}). * November ** {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|WD=Q11501518}} (November 24): A festival in which the emperor offers newly harvested grain to the deities and partakes of it himself, giving thanks for the harvest. * December ** Tsukinamisai (December 18–19) === Precincts === [[Image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya]] The shrine buildings of the four auxiliary shrines are nearly identical and, regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female, follow the Inner Shrine style: thatched Shinmei-zukuri facing south, with inward-cut chigi and an even number (six) of katsuogi. The old shrine sites for periodic rebuilding are usually adjacent east–west, but at Tsukiyomi-no-miya they are arranged north–south and are not adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii is also larger. * Tsukiyomi-no-miya – Auxiliary shrine of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine); the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine precinct. * Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya – Enshrined deity: Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanagi-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanami-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}} – Enshrined deities: Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto, {{ill|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama no Mionoya no Mikoto}}, and Ikarihime-no-Mikoto; all are considered deities of the five grains who protect fields and paddies. A subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. Ashihara Shrine follows the Inner Shrine style, with inward-cut chigi and four (even-numbered) katsuogi, in a board-roofed Shinmei-zukuri style. * Guardhouse === Access === * Nearest station: About a 10-minute walk south from {{ill|lt=Isuzugawa Station|Q6089533|WD=Q6089533}} on the {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Toba Line|Q5357612|WD=Q5357612}} of {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|WD=Q1531085}} :: About a 1-hour walk from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|WD=Q6079748}} on the {{ill|lt=Sangū Line|Q872023|WD=Q872023}} of {{ill|lt=JR Central|Q513679|WD=Q513679}} * Nearest bus stop: About a 5-minute walk from Nakamura-chō bus stop on the 51 Outer–Inner Shrine Line of {{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516|WD=Q6843516}} ({{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū Ise Office|Q11357667|WD=Q11357667}}) * Nearest interchange: About 1 km from {{ill|lt=Ise Interchange|Q10884857|WD=Q10884857}} on the {{ill|lt=Ise Expressway|Q6079578|WD=Q6079578}} * Roads: Along {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 37 Toba–Matsusaka Line|Q11357923|WD=Q11357923}} ({{ill|lt=Miyuki Road|Q22222736|WD=Q22222736}}) (main approach), and along {{ill|lt=National Route 23|Q5357579|WD=Q5357579}} (rear approach) * Parking: There is a large parking lot on the national road side that can accommodate buses; several cars can also be parked on the prefectural road side. === Notes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === References === * “Guide to Visiting the Four Auxiliary Shrines Including Tsukiyomi-no-miya” (published by the Jingu Administration Office) * “Walking around Oise-san” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) * “Oise Pilgrimage” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) === See also === {{Commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Naiku)}} * {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520}} * {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} * {{ill|lt=List of the 125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine|Q16482760|WD=Q16482760}} * {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|WD=Q328067}} {{125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine}} {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsukiyomi-no-miya}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Ronsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Subshrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:神宮125社]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社|大つきよみのみや]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:2014年竣工の日本の建築物]]

{{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} Auxiliary Shrine |Established = Before {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|lt=804|Q29998|WD=Q29998}}) |Main hall style = {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545}} |Annual festival = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=28|lat_sec=24.6|lon_deg=136|lon_min=43|lon_sec=43.8|label=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|28|24.6|N|136|43|43.8|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-miya''' (つきよみのみや) is a Shinto shrine located in Nakamura-chō, {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|WD=Q328067}}, {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|WD=Q128196}}. It is an auxiliary shrine (betsugū) of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=UNKNOWN}}. It is sometimes written with the abbreviated characters “月読宮”. At the 62nd {{ill|lt=Shikinen Sengū of Ise Grand Shrine|Q3959472|WD=Q3959472}}, the transfer of the deity ({{ill|lt=Sengu|Q24892914|WD=Q24892914}}) was performed at 8:00 p.m. on {{ill|lt=October 6|Q2928|WD=Q2928}}, {{ill|lt=2014|Q1999|WD=Q1999}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510}} 26), about one year after the transfer at the Inner Shrine{{Cite web|ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|title=“‘Divine works?’ Ise Grand Shrine’s ‘Sengu ceremony’ repeatedly avoids direct typhoon hits”|publisher={{ill|lt=Ise-Shima Keizai Shimbun|Q18700592|WD=Q18700592}}|date=2014-10-13|accessdate=2014-10-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019123119/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2151/|archivedate=2014-10-19}}. === Enshrined deities === {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt='''Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto'''}}{{Cite web |url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/ |title=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Auxiliary Shrine of the Inner Shrine) |accessdate=2024-03-09}} (つきよみのみこと) – the second worship hall from the right when facing Tsukiyomi-no-miya. '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama|1=UNKNOWN}}''' – the rightmost worship hall when facing Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya. '''{{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}''' – the third worship hall from the right when facing Isanagi-no-miya. '''{{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}''' – the leftmost worship hall when facing Isanami-no-miya. === Overview === [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the main approach entrance]] [[Image:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}}, a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine]] [[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Temizuya and guardhouse]] Tsukiyomi-no-miya is an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine located in Nakamura-chō along the middle reaches of the {{ill|lt=Isuzu River|Q6089522|WD=Q6089522}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|lt=Toyouke Daijingū|Q11633343|WD=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. It is also affectionately called “Tsukiyomi-san”; however, the enshrined deity “Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto” of {{ill|lt=Tsukiyo-mi-no-miya|Q11516023|WD=Q11516023}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine also called “Tsukiyomi-san,” is considered the same deity as that of the main auxiliary shrine. Within the precincts are three other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine: '''Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya''', which enshrines the aramitama (rough spirit) of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto; '''Isanagi-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; and '''Isanami-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}. Aside from Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings lined up is {{ill|lt=Takihara-no-miya|Q11566292|WD=Q11566292}}, which has two. The shrine buildings are comparable in scale to other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine except {{ill|lt=Aramatsuri-no-miya|Q2859485|WD=Q2859485}}; though smaller than the main sanctuary, the sight of four {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545}} shrine buildings standing in a row is magnificent. The transfer ceremonies were held for Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya at 10:00 p.m. on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya on {{ill|lt=October 10|Q2921|WD=Q2921}}. Old timbers from Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, dismantled in 2014, were donated to {{ill|lt=Yakumo Shrine (Ashikaga City)|Q11391850|WD=Q11391850|lt=Yakumo Shrine}} in Midori-chō, {{ill|lt=Ashikaga City|Q374477|WD=Q374477}}, {{ill|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843|WD=Q44843}}, which lost its main hall to a fire in {{ill|lt=2012|Q1990|WD=Q1990}} (Heisei 24){{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=“Long-awaited main hall at Yakumo Shrine—donated by Ise Grand Shrine”|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}}. From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, Tsukiyomi-no-miya, Isanagi-no-miya, and Isanami-no-miya; however, the correct order of worship is said to be Tsukiyomi-no-miya → Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya → Isanagi-no-miya → Isanami-no-miya. Because Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the younger sibling deity of the supreme deity {{ill|lt=Amaterasu|UNKNOWN|WD=|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, is enshrined here, Tsukiyomi-no-miya ranks second among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine after '''Aramatsuri-no-miya''', which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, and it is the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine’s main precinct. In addition to the four auxiliary shrines above, the precincts include '''{{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}}''', a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. As with other off-site auxiliary shrines, there is a guardhouse (shukueiya) staffed by priests during visiting hours, where talismans and amulets are bestowed and arrangements are made for kagura dances and food offerings. === History === Although the exact origins are unclear, the “Daijingū Gishikichō” records that in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|lt=804|Q29998|WD=Q29998}}) during the reign of the 50th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Kanmu|Q314846|WD=Q314846}}, “Tsukiyomi-no-miya, one compound, four main sanctuaries” were enshrined within a single sacred fence, and the four auxiliary shrines together were called “Tsukiyomi-no-miya.” In {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 9 ({{ill|lt=867|Q30347|WD=Q30347}}) during the reign of the 56th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|WD=Q349243}}, the shrine names Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya were granted. According to the {{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448}} of {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470}}) during the reign of the 60th emperor {{ill|lt=Emperor Daigo|Q329753|WD=Q329753}}, at that time Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya formed one compound enclosed by a sacred fence, and likewise Tsukiyomi-no-miya and Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya formed another. From {{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|WD=Q7757}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}} 6), all four shrines came to have their own individual sacred fences, forming the current layout. === Festivals === Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of the Inner Shrine, and for major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai, offerings (heihaku) are presented from the Imperial Household. * January ** Saitansai (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial line. ** {{ill|lt=Genshisai|Q11387821|WD=Q11387821}} (January 3): A festival celebrating the origin of the imperial succession at the start of the year. * February ** National Foundation Commemoration Festival (February 11): A festival celebrating the founding of the nation by {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188}}. ** {{ill|lt=Kinensai|Q118906710|WD=Q118906710}} (February 18): A festival praying for a bountiful harvest and national peace at the beginning of the year. ** Tenchōsai (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Naruhito|1=UNKNOWN}}. * May ** Kazahinomisai (May 14): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * June ** Tsukinamisai (June 18–19): A festival held in June and December praying for national peace and the emperor’s well-being; at Ise Grand Shrine it is, together with the Kannamesai, called one of the Three Seasonal Festivals. * August ** Kazahinomisai (August 4): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests. * October ** {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|WD=Q11255045}} (October 18–19): A festival in which priests offer newly harvested grain of the year as sacred food ({{ill|lt=Shinsen|Q11591045|WD=Q11591045|lt=Ōmike}}). * November ** {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|WD=Q11501518}} (November 24): A festival in which the emperor offers newly harvested grain to the deities and partakes of it himself, giving thanks for the harvest. * December ** Tsukinamisai (December 18–19) === Precincts === [[Image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya]] The shrine buildings of the four auxiliary shrines are nearly identical and, regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female, follow the Inner Shrine style: thatched Shinmei-zukuri facing south, with inward-cut chigi and an even number (six) of katsuogi. The old shrine sites for periodic rebuilding are usually adjacent east–west, but at Tsukiyomi-no-miya they are arranged north–south and are not adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii is also larger. * Tsukiyomi-no-miya – Auxiliary shrine of {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} {{ill|lt=Kōtaijingū|Q11581011|WD=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine); the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine precinct. * Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya – Enshrined deity: Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanagi-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * Isanami-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine. * {{ill|lt=Ashihara Shrine|Q17191305|WD=Q17191305}} – Enshrined deities: Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto, {{ill|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama no Mionoya no Mikoto}}, and Ikarihime-no-Mikoto; all are considered deities of the five grains who protect fields and paddies. A subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. Ashihara Shrine follows the Inner Shrine style, with inward-cut chigi and four (even-numbered) katsuogi, in a board-roofed Shinmei-zukuri style. * Guardhouse === Access === * Nearest station: About a 10-minute walk south from {{ill|lt=Isuzugawa Station|Q6089533|WD=Q6089533}} on the {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Toba Line|Q5357612|WD=Q5357612}} of {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|WD=Q1531085}} :: About a 1-hour walk from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|WD=Q6079748}} on the {{ill|lt=Sangū Line|Q872023|WD=Q872023}} of {{ill|lt=JR Central|Q513679|WD=Q513679}} * Nearest bus stop: About a 5-minute walk from Nakamura-chō bus stop on the 51 Outer–Inner Shrine Line of {{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516|WD=Q6843516}} ({{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū Ise Office|Q11357667|WD=Q11357667}}) * Nearest interchange: About 1 km from {{ill|lt=Ise Interchange|Q10884857|WD=Q10884857}} on the {{ill|lt=Ise Expressway|Q6079578|WD=Q6079578}} * Roads: Along {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 37 Toba–Matsusaka Line|Q11357923|WD=Q11357923}} ({{ill|lt=Miyuki Road|Q22222736|WD=Q22222736}}) (main approach), and along {{ill|lt=National Route 23|Q5357579|WD=Q5357579}} (rear approach) * Parking: There is a large parking lot on the national road side that can accommodate buses; several cars can also be parked on the prefectural road side. === Notes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === References === * “Guide to Visiting the Four Auxiliary Shrines Including Tsukiyomi-no-miya” (published by the Jingu Administration Office) * “Walking around Oise-san” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) * “Oise Pilgrimage” (published by the Ise Grand Shrine Association of Worshippers) === See also === {{Commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Naiku)}} * {{ill|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520}} * {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168}} * {{ill|lt=List of the 125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine|Q16482760|WD=Q16482760}} * {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|WD=Q328067}} {{125 Shrines of Ise Grand Shrine}} {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsukiyomi-no-miya}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Ronsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Subshrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:神宮125社]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社|大つきよみのみや]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:2014年竣工の日本の建築物]]
